0.long_answer: Michels syndrome, also known as 3MC syndrome, is characterized by craniosynostosis, which is the premature fusion of the fibrous joints in the skull. These fibrous joints, known as the calvarial sutures, include those like the coronal, sagittal, lambdoid, and metopic sutures that normally remain unfused to allow for proper skull and brain growth. In Michels syndrome, the premature ossification of these sutures restricts skull expansion and alters the normal growth and shape of the head and face.
